title: InterviewPrep AI curriculum audit manifest
description: Audited inventory of instructional tracks governed by the curriculum content contract.

outcomes: Explain activation-function behavior and its role in neural networks.
Choose an activation for a stated modeling constraint.
Explain how attention forms a weighted context.
Identify the compute and memory cost of attention.
Explain training and inference statistics in batch normalization.
Recognize when batch normalization is unsuitable.
Explain why accuracy can conceal minority-class failure.
Select a mitigation and metric for an imbalanced task.
Explain local receptive fields and parameter sharing.
Estimate convolution output shape and cost.
Choose a validation split that matches the data-generating process.
Explain leakage risks in cross-validation.
Distinguish training-only information from leakage.
Design a split and pipeline that prevent leakage.
Compare data and model parallelism.
Diagnose communication and scaling limits.
Describe covariate and label shift assumptions.
Choose an adaptation strategy and validation plan.
Explain dropout as stochastic regularization.
Apply train and inference behavior correctly.
Interpret validation curves for stopping decisions.
Avoid selecting a stopping point on test data.
Explain how diversity affects ensemble gains.
Choose between bagging, boosting, and stacking.
Match metrics to costs and class balance.
Explain threshold-dependent and threshold-free metrics.
Build features without crossing split boundaries.
Evaluate representation choices against model and data constraints.
Relate accumulated gradients to a larger effective batch.
Identify optimizer and normalization caveats.
Compare grid, random, and adaptive search.
Budget tuning while avoiding validation overfit.
Explain soft-target distillation and temperature.
Choose teacher and student evaluation criteria.
Compare normalization axes and batch dependence.
Choose normalization for sequence and small-batch settings.
Explain common learning-rate schedules.
Select a schedule and stopping criterion for a training budget.
Relate an objective to the prediction task.
Identify objective mismatch and robustness issues.
Explain learning-to-learn and few-shot adaptation.
Distinguish task distribution assumptions from ordinary generalization.
Explain precision, range, and loss scaling trade-offs.
Recognize numerical overflow and underflow symptoms.
Compare compression methods by resource and quality impact.
Choose a deployment-aware evaluation metric.
Select a model using validation evidence and constraints.
Explain selection bias from repeated experimentation.
Explain momentum updates and their smoothing effect.
Diagnose overshoot and unstable optimization.
Derive a Naive Bayes decision from Bayes rule.
Explain the conditional-independence assumption and its practical limits.
Describe a feed-forward network as composed functions.
Relate capacity, data, and regularization choices.
Explain gradient-based objective minimization.
Diagnose learning-rate and conditioning problems.
Interpret train-validation gaps as evidence about generalization.
Choose a mitigation that addresses the observed failure.
Use conditional probability to reason about model predictions.
Explain sampling uncertainty in evaluation results.
Compare structured and unstructured pruning.
Evaluate sparsity against actual deployment support.
Explain quantization scales and calibration data.
Measure accuracy and resource changes after quantization.
Explain how a penalty changes the fitting objective.
Choose a regularizer based on the expected failure mode.
Explain recurrent state and gated updates.
Compare sequential recurrence with parallel sequence models.
Distinguish supervised prediction tasks by target type.
Describe a valid train-validation-test workflow.
Explain margins and support vectors.
Choose a kernel model with awareness of scaling and dataset size.
Compare feature extraction and fine-tuning.
Detect negative transfer and domain mismatch.
Describe transformer blocks and positional information.
Reason about attention cost and sequence-length limits.
Distinguish clustering, density, and representation objectives.
Evaluate unsupervised results without assuming labels.
Explain signal propagation at initialization.
Choose initialization based on activation and layer dimensions.
Construct a bootstrap interval using the correct resampling unit.
Identify sample and dependence conditions where bootstrap inference is unreliable.
Construct randomization distributions under a stated null.
Preserve the experiment assignment structure in permutations.
Define a family of tests and select an error criterion.
Apply FDR control and explain its dependence assumptions.
Distinguish MCAR, MAR, and MNAR assumptions.
Choose and diagnose an estimator for missing outcomes under explicit assumptions.
Diagnose residual patterns, heteroskedasticity, and influence.
Choose uncertainty estimates that reflect the sampling dependence structure.
Explain how unadjusted repeated looks inflate false-positive probability.
Specify a valid stopping and error-control plan for sequential experimentation.
Explain top-k routing, capacity and overflow.
Diagnose load imbalance from assignment and gate statistics.
Compare context allocation strategies under a token budget.
Evaluate evidence coverage and answer support across context positions.
Account for speculative acceptance and rejection.
Estimate break-even behavior without confusing formulas with measured speed.
Calculate KV cache memory from model and sequence dimensions.
Explain safe prefix reuse and eviction behavior.
Construct and validate causal sparse masks.
Choose a pattern based on reachability and kernel support.
Separate quantization and student approximation error.
Compare quality, storage and measured target-runtime behavior.
Implement late fusion with explicit missing-modality behavior.
Evaluate calibration and disagreement across modality subsets.
Distinguish TTFT, decode time and queue delay.
Compare scheduling designs with tail latency and transfer cost.
Classify behavior and knowledge gaps before selecting adaptation.
Compare prompt, retrieval, adapter and full tuning with held-out evaluation.
Calibrate output-length predictions and quantify underprediction.
Choose tail-aware reservations and validate their scheduler impact.
Define service, data and delayed quality indicators with owners and response actions.
Compute windowed rates and suppress alerts with insufficient evidence.
Distinguish feature distribution shifts from changes in labeled outcomes.
Choose a drift statistic, threshold and validation response for a production signal.
Order dependent pipeline tasks and resume completed work safely.
Bound a backfill by partitions and explain idempotency and retry requirements.
Compare offline and online feature values and freshness.
Diagnose parity failures using event time, observed time and mismatch rates.
Set rollback triggers using service health and sufficiently mature quality labels.
Coordinate incident containment, evidence capture and safe recovery.
Validate required lineage fields for a reproducible model release.
Create stable fingerprints and explain audit evidence limits.
Apply least-privilege authorization and redact sensitive fields.
Choose retention actions that respect policy and legal holds.
Estimate monthly serving cost and capacity with explicit headroom.
Choose a budget response while preserving reliability objectives.
